headline: Bank of Canada Holds at 2.25% for a Fourth Time as Q4 GDP Contracts 0.6% and Oil Hits $100 on the Strait of Hormuz Disruption

facts.statement: The Bank of Canada held the overnight rate at 2.25% on April 29, 2026 — its fourth consecutive hold, unchanged since October 2025. Governing Council said it would look through the war's immediate inflation impact but "will not let higher energy prices become persistent inflation," projecting a return to the 2% target in 2027.
facts.source_title: Bank of Canada maintains policy rate at 2.25%
connections: 211 residential projects ($32.2B) and 1,663 infrastructure projects ($210.3B) carry rate-sensitive financing

facts.statement: Real GDP contracted 0.6% annualized in Q4 2025 against a consensus expectation of flat output; full-year 2025 growth was 1.7%, the slowest pace since 2016 excluding the pandemic. Lower exports, particularly to the U.S. under steel, aluminum and motor-vehicle tariffs, were the main drag.
facts.source_title: Recent developments in the Canadian economy: Spring 2026 — StatCan
connections: Manufacturing GDP -3.1% YoY; 83 manufacturing projects ($129.0B) tracked
Three in ten manufacturers reported a major negative tariff impact; one in five plan to delay investment

facts.statement: WTI crude settled near $100.16/bbl (+5.0% on the week, +60.1% year-over-year) and Brent at $108.59 (+7.2% wk) as the Strait of Hormuz disruption cut ~4 million bpd of flows in March-April. The IEA described the disruption as exceeding the 1970s oil crises in scale.
connections: March CPI gasoline component +21.2% M/M, the largest monthly increase on record

facts.statement: Headline CPI rose 2.4% year-over-year in March 2026, up from 1.8% in February, lifted by the record monthly gasoline increase. Inflation remains within the Bank of Canada's 1-3% target band.
facts.source_title: Consumer Price Index, March 2026 — Statistics Canada
connections: BoC projects inflation returning to 2% in 2027
GoC yields backed up ~5-7 bps on the week as energy-driven inflation re-priced

facts.statement: Canada posted a $1.8B merchandise trade surplus in March — its first since September 2025 — reversing a $5.1B February deficit. The surplus with the U.S. widened to $7.1B as exports to the U.S. rose 8.3%, led by crude oil and passenger vehicles; non-U.S. exports hit an all-time high (+9.1% M/M).
facts.source_title: Canadian international merchandise trade, March 2026 — Statistics Canada
connections: 390 mining projects ($227.1B) and 59 oil_gas projects ($97.6B) tracked
Metal/mineral and energy products posted the largest non-U.S. export increases

facts.statement: Unemployment rose to 6.9% in April from 6.7% in March, with 18,000 jobs lost; youth unemployment reached 14.3% and the long-term unemployment share was 22.5%. The employment rate eased to 60.5% while participation held at 65.0%.
facts.source_title: Labour Force Survey, April 2026 — Statistics Canada
connections: Indeed Hiring Lab characterized the labour market as "stuck in neutral"

facts.statement: CMHC's March housing-starts monthly SAAR fell 6% to 235,852 units from 250,961 in February; the six-month trend eased to 248,378. Actual starts in centres of 10,000+ population were 16,398 units, +10% year-over-year, with Montreal +26%, Toronto +23% and Vancouver +21%.
connections: 211 residential projects ($32.2B) and 1,663 infrastructure projects ($210.3B) tracked
Multi-unit construction drove the large-city YoY gains

Rate held at 2.25%; 1,663 infrastructure ($210.3B) + 211 residential ($32.2B) + 212 commercial-adjacent projects carry rate-sensitive financing exposure.

key_developments: Federal Reserve held the fed funds target at 3.50%-3.75% on April 29, 2026 — third consecutive hold.
FOMC statement cited elevated inflation "in part reflecting the recent increase in global energy prices."
Powell's likely final meeting as Chair; Kevin Warsh appointment effective May 15, 2026.
Markets pricing no Fed changes through the rest of 2026 and into 2027.
global_package.canada_impact: The wide Fed-BoC differential (3.50%-3.75% vs 2.25%) supports a softer Canadian dollar despite high crude prices. Solid U.S. growth sustains Canadian export demand even amid steel, aluminum and motor-vehicle tariffs.

global_package.canada_impact: Resilient Chinese demand supports copper (+37.3% YoY in timeseries), iron ore and energy export prices; the potash/canola channel is relevant qualitatively (no timeseries series tracked).

key_developments: ECB held all three key rates on April 30, 2026 (deposit 2.00%, MRO 2.15%, marginal lending 2.40%).
Bloomberg-surveyed economists expect two ECB quarter-point hikes in 2026 (June and September) as the war drives inflation higher.
Energy-driven global inflation regime in focus.
global_package.canada_impact: Potential ECB tightening supports the euro and global yields, reinforcing the back-up in Government of Canada yields (~5-7 bps on the week).

key_developments: Bank of England held Bank Rate at 3.75% on April 30, 2026 — second consecutive hold, third decision without a cut; MPC voted 8-1.
Confirms a synchronized G7 "hold" stance through April amid the energy shock.
global_package.canada_impact: The synchronized G7 hold and energy-shock backdrop support global term-premium repricing, reflected in higher Government of Canada yields.

StatCan March gasoline +21.2% month over month (record), +5.9% YoY.
Wages have outpaced prices for 3+ years (SEPH +3.9%), partially offsetting cost pressure.
Rental affordability improving — national rent-to-income ratio fell to 29%, below the 30% threshold for the first time in 6+ years; average rent -5.3% YoY to $2,008.
Mortgage stress: lowest 5-year fixed ~4.04%, edging up as energy-driven inflation lifts fixed rates; 70% of prospective buyers say conditions are too uncertain to judge timing.
Labour-market unease: 18,000 jobs lost in April, unemployment 6.9%, youth unemployment 14.3%, long-term unemployment share 22.5%.
